claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and a 3% rollout with rollback and monitoring provides sufficient control, with certification being supportable if the known health-plan benefits support limitation is disclosed at launch.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor summary states the health-plan benefits support use case remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The actor summary also states there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
No admissible evidence in the provided record shows that launch-time model-card disclosure has actually been approved, completed, or attached to the certification action.
The recommended action is an unconditional 'certify_model,' but the support described is conditional on disclosure; that predicate is unresolved in the available evidence.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant without separate admissible evidence that the required launch-time disclosure will occur.
That rollout at 3%, rollback, and monitoring are sufficient by themselves to cure the known material weakness.
That the certification decision, as locked, is fully supported rather than only conditionally supportable.
evidence_requests: Provide the final launch model card or equivalent disclosure artifact showing the health-plan benefits support limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide approval or sign-off records tying that disclosure artifact to this certification decision before launch.
Provide evidence that the affected use case is excluded from the initial rollout cohort, or an approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the material limitation is explicitly disclosed at launch and that disclosure is part of the certification record, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows the affected use case is excluded from exposure, the disclosure predicate may change under the stated policy.
If an approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed segment exists, the verdict could improve.
Absent disclosure, exclusion, or approved risk acceptance, certification remains unsupported under the stated policy.
